title: Several penny stocks are down 36% to 68%, and two have reverse splits
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
Today's write-ups flag a group of low-priced names with 30-day  
declines of about 68%, 39% and 36%, plus two reverse splits.  
  
These are high-risk names. Here is what those write-ups show, not a  
recommendation to trade them.  
  
\*\*1. Ping An Biomedical (PASW)\*\* — PASW shares fell roughly 68% over  
the trailing 30 days, sliding from about $4.72 to $1.53 on a  
split-adjusted basis. The decline followed a 1-for-40 reverse stock  
split, a $300 million shelf registration, and a low-near-term-revenue  
patent acquisition, all set against extremely thin trading liquidity.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/ping-an-biomedical-pasw-drops-68-over-30-days-after-reverse-split-38666/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/ping-an-biomedical-pasw-drops-68-over-30-days-after-reverse-split-38666/)  
  
\*\*2. Microbot Medical (MBOT)\*\* — MBOT is at $0.60, down -38.78% from  
Friday's $0.98 close; the decline came in Monday's regular session,  
with shares gapping to $0.65 at the open and trading as low as $0.53.  
The catalyst is the third-quarter 2026 report: revenue fell to $72,000  
from $241,000 in Q2, EPS came in at -$0.09, and gross margin turned  
negative on an $815,000 inventory write-down, signaling  
slower-than-expected LIBERTY adoption.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-microbot-medical-inc-mbot-stock-down-38-78-today-38786/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-microbot-medical-inc-mbot-stock-down-38-78-today-38786/)  
  
\*\*3. Enovix (ENVX)\*\* — Enovix shares fell roughly 36% over the last 30  
days, sliding from about $2.49 to a close near $1.60. The decline  
accelerated after third-quarter 2026 results, as a delayed smartphone  
program and soft fourth-quarter guidance outweighed revenue that beat  
estimates.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/enovix-envx-slides-36-in-30-days-execution-concerns-weigh-on-shares-38461/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/enovix-envx-slides-36-in-30-days-execution-concerns-weigh-on-shares-38461/)  
  
\*\*4. The Children's Place (PLCE)\*\* — PLCE dropped -35.81% during the  
regular session, falling from a $0.444 close to $0.285, surrendering  
most of the prior day's rebound on heavy turnover. No verified news or  
fundamental catalyst found: no company release or SEC filing  
accompanied the reversal, which retraced part of the previous  
session's +123.68% speculative surge — consistent with profit-taking  
in a heavily shorted, sub-dollar Chapter 11 equity.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-the-children-s-place-plce-stock-down-35-81-today-38790/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-the-children-s-place-plce-stock-down-35-81-today-38790/)  
  
\*\*5. Veritone (VERI)\*\* — VERI dropped from a $0.4516 close on November  
13 to $0.304, a -32.68% decline, with selling starting in premarket  
after the 8:30 a.m. ET release and extending through regular trading  
on November 16. The trigger was a badly missed third quarter: revenue  
of $18.6 million fell -30.1% year over year and came in far below the  
roughly $34 million consensus, while annual recurring revenue slipped  
\-12.6% to $55.9 million.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-veritone-inc-veri-stock-down-32-68-today-38792/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-veritone-inc-veri-stock-down-32-68-today-38792/)  
  
\*\*6. Focus Universal (FCUV)\*\* — Focus Universal (FCUV) dropped from  
Friday's close of $7.08 to $4.93, a -30.37% decline, in early  
regular-session trading on Monday. No verified news or fundamental  
catalyst found; the pullback is consistent with profit-taking after  
Friday's +136% run, with the stock's typical daily move over the past  
60 sessions averaging roughly 9%.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-focus-universal-fcuv-stock-down-30-37-today-38791/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-focus-universal-fcuv-stock-down-30-37-today-38791/)  
  
\*\*7. Mannatech (MTEX)\*\* — MTEX dropped -27.62% to $4.56 in Monday's  
regular session from Friday's $6.30 close, extending a two-day  
collapse that has cut the share price roughly in half. The decline  
traces to the Nov. 12 Q3 report: sales fell -14.6% to $24.9 million,  
operating income dropped -86% to $0.3 million, and $8.9 million of net  
income came solely from a $10.9 million non-cash tax benefit.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-mannatech-mtex-stock-down-31-11-today-38805/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-mannatech-mtex-stock-down-31-11-today-38805/)  
  
\*\*8. LanzaTech Global (LNZA)\*\* — LNZA fell from Friday's $3.85 close  
to $2.80, a -27.27% drop during Monday's regular session. The decline  
followed third-quarter results released before the opening bell: a net  
loss of $178.0M versus $2.9M of income a year earlier, driven by a  
$166.4M non-cash fair-value loss on its SGLT stake, with a GAAP loss  
of $13.60 per share and revenue up only +2% to $9.5M.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-lanzatech-global-lnza-stock-down-27-79-today-38799/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-lanzatech-global-lnza-stock-down-27-79-today-38799/)  
  
\*\*9. [Myseum.AI](http://Myseum.AI) (MYSE)\*\* — The $1.50 central target is a technical  
recovery milestone tied to the $1.40–$1.50 zone where MYSE  
consolidated in early-to-mid October 2026, not an analyst consensus.  
Target, not a promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/myseum-ai-myse-could-the-stock-recover-toward-1-50-46-upside-38476/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/myseum-ai-myse-could-the-stock-recover-toward-1-50-46-upside-38476/)  
  
\*\*10. Alps Group (ALPS)\*\* — Alps Group (ALPS) shares declined roughly  
30.6% over the last 30 days, falling from a close near $1.70 in  
mid-October to about $1.18 by mid-November.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/alps-group-alps-declines-30-6-over-30-days-as-reverse-split-takes-effect-38469/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/alps-group-alps-declines-30-6-over-30-days-as-reverse-split-takes-effect-38469/)  
  
\*\*11. Aligos Therapeutics (ALGS)\*\* — The $60 central target is the  
arithmetic mean of six verified analyst price targets — not an  
official published consensus figure. At roughly $2.10 per share,  
Aligos Therapeutics would need a gain of about 2,757% to reach $60, an  
exceptionally large move. Target, not a promise.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/aligos-therapeutics-algs-60-target-would-require-2-757-gain-from-current-levels-38528/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/aligos-therapeutics-algs-60-target-would-require-2-757-gain-from-current-levels-38528/)  
  
\*\*12. Forcendra Holding (FCDH)\*\* — FCDH fell -29.41% in Monday's  
regular session, sliding from Friday's $0.68 close to $0.48 and  
erasing most of the prior session's +35.97% advance. The driver is  
Forcendra's 1-for-5 reverse share split, announced November 13 and  
effective today at 4:30 PM ET; holders are exiting positions built  
during Friday's split-driven spike, and no new company release or  
filing appeared today.  
  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-forcendra-holding-limited-fcdh-stock-down-32-69-today-38783/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-forcendra-holding-limited-fcdh-stock-down-32-69-today-38783/)  
  
Do you avoid names like these after a reverse split, or is there one  
in this list you still want to understand better?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from today's (Nov 16) write-ups,  
using intraday or latest-close prices, not live quotes. Price targets  
are targets, not promises.
